observations: Photo 0 and photo 1 show the same teal-and-cream industrial machine from two angles, apparently a thread book-sewing / signature-sewing machine used in bookbinding.
Machine has multiple sewing heads, a feed table, a control panel with buttons, and a rotary power switch.
Visible wear: rust on metal feed plate, grime on frame, dust and dirt on floor and casing.
No manufacturer nameplate, serial number, or model text is legible in either photo.
A watermark 'OYOLAKFOM NIGLTD POSTED ON JIJI' overlays both images; this is a listing watermark, not a machine brand.
A person is visible in the background of photo 0, suggesting the photo was taken in a working shop/warehouse.
No power cable connection to an outlet is visible, and no photo shows the machine running or stitching paper.

claims.evidence: No photo or video shows the machine powered on, running, or producing stitched output; no close-up of the control panel display or motor plate is given.

risks.risk: Machine may not power on or have a working motor/electrical system.
risks.proof: A video clip of the machine being switched on and running a sewing cycle.

risks.risk: Missing or damaged internal parts (needles, thread guides, timing belts) not visible from exterior photos.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the sewing heads and internal mechanism with covers open.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / needing parts

risks.risk: No brand/model/serial identifiable, so capacity, year, and original spec are unknown, affecting resale value.
risks.proof: Clear photo of any nameplate, serial tag, or manufacturer sticker on the frame or control box.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic unbranded used unit

risks.risk: Visible rust and grime suggest possible long periods of disuse or storage in a damp environment, which can affect internal components.
risks.proof: Photos of internal rollers, gears, and sewing heads showing rust or corrosion state.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working, heavy wear assumed

proof_requests: Video of the machine running a full sewing/stitching cycle with material feeding through.
Close-up photo of any nameplate, serial number, or model sticker on the machine body or control panel.
Photos with covers/panels open showing the internal sewing heads and mechanism.
Photo of the power cable connected to an outlet and the control panel lit up.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable by type as a used industrial book-sewing machine, but the seller's 'perfect working condition' claim is unverifiable from static photos with no running demonstration, so it must be priced at worst case as non-working/unverified until proof is given.
